title: Cap. VIII Resp.: personal unworthiness foresighted — but not antecedent motive of the reprobation decree
pass_a_gloss: In this sentence, if speech be only of adults, we will concede to Arminius and Corvinus that a certain personal and proper unworthiness, sprung from voluntary rebellion, was foresighted from eternity in all those whom God from eternity reprobated: but we will deny that from this foresighted actual and final rebellion of the same the decree of reprobation flowed as from an antecedent and moving cause. Nay rather we affirm that in the Divine will that decree of permissive hardening or of reprobation, of which the Apostle so speaks, He will have mercy on whom he will, and whom he will he hardens, ought to be conceived by us prior, before we can conceive in the Divine mind that foresight related unto any singular person, by which from eternity God regards the same person as struggling against his grace, and unto the end of his life contumaciously spurning and rejecting the same grace.
pass_b_english: If the talk is of adults only, we grant Arminius and Corvinus this much: a certain personal proper unworthiness, sprung from voluntary rebellion, was foresighted from eternity in all whom God from eternity reprobated. What we deny is that from that foresighted actual and final rebellion the reprobation decree flowed as from an antecedent moving cause. Rather we affirm: in the divine will we must first conceive that decree of permissive hardening or reprobation of which Paul speaks — He has mercy on whom he will, and whom he will he hardens — before we can conceive in the divine mind that foresight of any particular person as from eternity struggling against his grace and, to life's end, contumaciously spurning and rejecting it.
source_text: In hac sententia, si de adultis solis sermo sit, concedemus Arminio et Corvino, personalem ac propriam quandam indignitatem, ex voluntaria rebellione ortam, fuisse in illis omnibus ab aeterno praevisam, quos Deus ab aeterno reprobavit: sed negabimus, ex praevisa hac actuali et finali eorundem rebellione decretum reprobationis, tanquam ex causa antecedanea et motiva, emanasse. Quin potius affirmamus, in voluntate Divina prius concipi a nobis oportere decretum illud indurationis permissivae sive reprobationis, de qua Apostolus sic loquitur, Miserebitur cujus vult, et quem vult indurat, quam in mente Divina concipere possimus praevisionem istam ad quamlibet singularem personam relatam, qua ab aeterno Deus intuetur eandem personam ut gratiae suae reluctantem, et ad finem usque vitae suae eandem gratiam contumaciter aspernantem et rejicientem.
